lines: Two function generators, each also a slew limiter and an envelope follower, feeding four attenuverter channels and a mixing bus that sums, inverts and takes the maximum
Sets how long that channel's rise takes, from a tenth of a millisecond at the far left to 1500 seconds at the far right
Sets how long that channel's fall takes, from a tenth of a millisecond at the far left to 1500 seconds at the far right
Bends both slopes of that channel: logarithmic at the far left, linear a third of the way up, exponential at the far right; the left half also stretches the stage times, the right half shortens them
Picks how CURVE is applied to that channel: Shark Fin bends the rise and the fall in opposite directions, Mirror bends both the same way, and Mirror is the position it starts in
Latches that channel into free running, so it retriggers itself the moment the fall ends; the lamp beside it is lit while looping
An attenuverter on that generator's output, silent at centre, full level clockwise and full level inverted anticlockwise; it feeds the numbered output below it and the mixing bus
An attenuverter on IN 2, silent at centre, full level clockwise and inverted anticlockwise; with IN 2 unpatched it scales a fixed 10V, giving a manual offset from -10V to +10V
An attenuverter on IN 3, silent at centre, full level clockwise and inverted anticlockwise; with IN 3 unpatched it scales a fixed 5V, giving a manual offset from -5V to +5V
A signal for that channel to slew; while the generator is idle the channel tracks this voltage at the rates set by SURGE and SINK, and while a cycle is running it is folded in gently instead
A rising edge above 1V starts a fresh rise on that channel; an edge during the rise is ignored, and one during the fall drops the output to 0V and restarts
A signal scaled by the attenuverter above it and sent to output 2 and the mixing bus; with nothing patched the channel reads a fixed 10V
A signal scaled by the attenuverter above it and sent to output 3 and the mixing bus; with nothing patched the channel reads a fixed 5V
Lengthens that channel's rise by half an octave of time per volt, and shortens it for negative voltage, over a span of twelve octaves either way
Lengthens that channel's fall by half an octave of time per volt, and shortens it for negative voltage, over a span of twelve octaves either way
Scales the rise and the fall of that channel together, positive voltage making the whole cycle faster and negative voltage slower
A voltage above 2.5V puts that channel into free running for as long as it is held, whatever the LOOP button is set to
That generator's output scaled by the attenuverter above it, clamped to ±10V; patching this jack takes the channel out of the OR, SUM and INV bus
IN 2 scaled by the attenuverter above it, clamped to ±10V; patching this jack takes the channel out of the OR, SUM and INV bus
IN 3 scaled by the attenuverter above it, clamped to ±10V; patching this jack takes the channel out of the OR, SUM and INV bus
A 10V gate on channel 1, going high at the top of the rise and staying high for the whole of the fall; with IN 1 patched and no cycle running it is high while the slew falls
A 10V gate on channel 4, high for the whole of the rise; with IN 4 patched and no cycle running it is high while the slew rises
That generator's output at full level, ahead of its attenuverter, swinging from 0V to 10.2V
The highest of the four channel voltages after their attenuverters, floored at 0V and clamped to 10V, counting only channels whose numbered output is unpatched
The four channel voltages after their attenuverters added together and clamped to ±10V, counting only channels whose numbered output is unpatched
The SUM voltage with its sign flipped, clamped to ±10V
Note — both attenuverters start at centre, where they pass nothing, so the numbered outputs and the mixing bus are silent until you turn one of them away from noon
Note — the two dark rectangles draw the shape of each channel's cycle, with a dot running along it while the channel is active; nothing on them can be clicked or dragged
Note — a channel with nothing patched into its signal or trigger jack and its LOOP button off holds at 0V; it needs a trigger, a loop or a patched signal before it puts anything out
Menu — Bandlimited EOR/EOC — smooths the edges of the EoR and EoC gates so they alias less at audio rates
Menu — Bandlimited CH1/CH4 Signal Outputs — smooths the jump the generator makes when a fall reaches the bottom, so the output aliases less at audio rates
Menu — Preview Tracer — draws a moving dot on each channel's curve display showing where that channel is in its cycle
Menu — Interpolate Timing Updates — spreads a change of rise or fall time across the samples between timing updates, removing the zipper tone heavy modulation otherwise causes
Menu — Timing Update Rate — sets how often the rise and fall times are recalculated from the knobs and the CV, at audio rate or one sample in four, eight, sixteen or thirty-two
Menu — Force Halo Dynamic Surface to NanoVG — draws the lit rings around the knobs without OpenGL

IntegralFlux.notes: Commit c37193d on branch puffy-rc3 carries version 2.9.1 and a plugin.json byte-identical to the installed one; that is the build read. The module is a Make Noise Maths emulation and the maker keeps the Maths manual in doc/manuals. Panel lettering names the rise and fall controls SURGE and SINK and the shape control CURVE, while the maker's tooltips call them rise, fall and shape; the lines follow the panel. The shape-mode switch carries no printed label. EoR on channel 1 is high for the whole of the fall and EoC on channel 4 is high for the whole of the rise, which is the Maths behaviour but is not what either abbreviation suggests. Self-cycling is held to 1000Hz and external triggering to 2000Hz by enforceOuterSpeedLimit, which stretches both stage times when the pair would run faster. The curve previews and the crystal button are plain widgets with no parameter behind them, so no click on them reaches this feature.

Proc.notes: One channel of Integral Flux with a HALT input added and the mixing bus removed. Panel lettering names the controls INPUT, TRIG, LOOP, SURGE, BOTH, HALT, SINK and CURVE; the maker's tooltips call them Signal, Trigger, Cycle, Surge, Both CV, Halt CV, Sink and Curve, and the amplitude knob carries no printed label at all. HALT is checked as a level and makes processChannel return before anything is written, so the output and both gates freeze rather than falling to zero. The amplitude knob is applied only while a cycle is running: the slew path sets signalOutputGain back to 1, so a slewed signal passes at full level whatever the knob says. Self-cycling is held to 1000Hz and external triggering to 2000Hz. There is no loop CV jack on this module, only the button.

lines: A stereo turntable: it records what you play into a circular buffer and gives you a platter you can drag, freeze, reverse and slip, or loads a sound file to play instead
Sets how far back into the recording the playhead may travel, from none of it at the far left to the whole buffer at the far right; with a sample loaded it sets where the playback window ends
Scales how far a drag on the platter moves the playhead, half as far at the far left and twice as far at the far right
Keeps the recording running underneath while you move the platter, so releasing it returns the playhead to where the sound would have been; the menu sets how quickly it rejoins
Sets the playback speed, half speed at the far left, normal speed at centre and double speed at the far right; a cable in the RATE jack takes this knob out of the calculation entirely
Runs the playhead backwards; with a cable in the REV jack and Reverse CV set to Gated Control the direction follows the cable and this button does nothing
Stops the playhead and stops recording, holding whatever is in the buffer; with a cable in the FREEZE jack and Freeze CV set to Gated Control the state follows the cable and this button does nothing
Crossfades the outputs between the signal arriving at IN L and IN R and the sound coming off the buffer, dry at the far left and buffer only at the far right
Mixes the output back into what is being written to the buffer, so material repeats and builds up; at the far left nothing is fed back
Steps through the cartridge characters, which change the tone of the sound read off the platter
Adds a TD.Scope expander to the right of this module
The left channel of the signal written into the buffer
The right channel of the signal written into the buffer
Sets the playback speed, half speed at -10V, normal speed at 0V and double speed at +10V; while a cable is in this jack the RATE knob is ignored, so a cable resting at 0V pins the speed to normal
Moves the playhead while the scratch gate is high, one second of recording per volt, positive voltage moving forward toward the newest sound in the buffer and negative deeper into the past
A voltage above 1V hands the playhead to the POS jack for as long as it is held, and starts the scratch gesture that S.GATE and S.POS report
A voltage above 1V stops the playhead and stops recording; crossing below -1V instead sends the playhead back to the start of the buffer
A voltage above 1V runs the playhead backwards; in Gated Control it holds the direction for as long as it is high, in Pulsed Control each rising edge flips it
The left channel of the mix of the input signal and the sound coming off the buffer, set by WET
The right channel of the mix of the input signal and the sound coming off the buffer, set by WET
10V for as long as a scratch gesture is running, whether it came from dragging the platter, dragging a TD.Scope waveform or the GATE jack, and 0V otherwise
How far the playhead has moved since the scratch gesture began, one volt per second, positive meaning toward the newest sound; it reads 0V whenever S.GATE is low
Note — the round platter is a single drawn widget rather than a control: drag it to move the playhead, and nothing on it can be clicked for its own note
Note — the module records whatever arrives at IN L and IN R from the moment it is placed, so with nothing patched in and no sample loaded there is nothing in the buffer to play
Note — to play a sound file instead of the incoming signal, load it from the menu; the buffer, the platter and every transport control then work on the file
Menu — Load sample... — opens a file chooser for a WAV, FLAC or MP3 to play in place of what the module records
Menu — Clear sample — discards the loaded file and returns the module to recording its inputs
Menu — Convert live -> sample — freezes what is currently in the buffer into a loaded sample, so it stops being overwritten
Menu — Save sample... — writes a sample made from the buffer to a WAV file
Menu — Sample info — shows the loaded file's name and length, and says so when it was cut short to fit the buffer
Menu — Buffer range: 10 s, 20 s, 1 min stereo, 2 min stereo, 10 min stereo, 10 min mono — sets how much recording is held, and so how much memory the module takes
Menu — Scratch interpolation: Cubic, 6-point Lagrange, Sinc (CPU heavy) — picks the arithmetic used to read between samples while scratching, trading tone for processor time
Menu — HQ rate interpolation — uses the better arithmetic for ordinary playback as well as for scratching
Menu — Gate+Pos mode: Module sync, Glide / inertia — sets whether the POS jack snaps the playhead to its voltage or glides toward it
Menu — Reverse CV: Gated Control, Pulsed Control — sets whether the REV jack holds the direction while high or flips it on each rising edge
Menu — Freeze CV: Gated Control, Pulsed Control — sets whether the FREEZE jack holds the freeze while high or toggles it on each rising edge
Menu — Slip return speed: None, Slow, Normal, Instant — sets how quickly the playhead rejoins the newest point in the recording after a slip, or turns slip off
Menu — Vinyl — chooses the artwork drawn on the platter and its brightness, and downloads the maker's library of platter art

TemporalDeck.notes: The RATE jack replaces the RATE knob rather than adding to it: computeBaseSpeed reads baseSpeedFromCv when the jack is connected and never looks at the knob, so a patched cable sitting at 0V holds normal speed and leaves the knob dead. The FREEZE and REV buttons are likewise inert whenever their jack is patched and the matching menu mode is Gated Control, which is the mode both come up in. The knob range and the CV range differ: the knob covers half to double speed across its travel, and the jack covers the same span across -10V to +10V. The FREEZE jack has a second function the panel does not show, and the maker's own tooltip does: crossing below -1V resets the playhead to the start of the buffer. The platter is an OpaqueWidget with no ParamWidget behind it, so dragging it works but no click on it reaches this feature; the same is true of the TD.Scope waveform. The cartridge and scope-spawn buttons carry no printed label.

lines: An expander for Temporal Deck that draws the buffer as a scrolling waveform, and lets you drag that waveform to move the playhead
Note — it works only when placed immediately to the right of a Temporal Deck; on its own the screen stays dark and dragging it does nothing
Note — drag the waveform up or down to move Temporal Deck's playhead, the same gesture as turning the platter; the amber band across the picture marks where the playhead is
Note — there are no jacks and no knobs on this module: everything it shows comes from the Temporal Deck beside it, and everything you can set is on its right-click menu
Menu — Mono — draws one waveform made from both channels
Menu — Stereo (side-by-side) — draws the left and right channels as two waveforms next to each other
Menu — Inverted Vertical — flips the picture top to bottom, so the newest sound is drawn at the other end
Menu — Scope Range: Auto (window peak), +/-2.5V full width, +/-5V full width, +/-10V full width — sets the voltage that fills the width of the display, or scales it to the loudest part on screen
Menu — Colors: Default (Purple/Cyan), Classic (Green/Red), Monochrome (Gray/White), Fire (Red/Yellow), Retro Amber, Retro Green — picks the colour scheme the waveform is drawn in
Menu — Brightness — a slider setting how bright the waveform is drawn
TDScope.notes: Leviathan 2.9.1 source (commit c37193d, branch puffy-rc3): TDScope.cpp declares no parameters, inputs or outputs at all, only two lights, so the entry is a first line, notes and menu items. It reads leftExpander.module and checks it is a Temporal Deck, which means it goes to the RIGHT of the deck. The waveform is a plain display widget with drag handling of its own; no click on it reaches this feature. The Debug Render submenu is only built when the maker's debug flag is set and is left out.

lines: An oscillator giving a sine wave, a morphing wave that grows a spike out of that sine, and a square one octave down

Undertow.notes: The MORPH CV jack multiplies the MORPH knob instead of adding to it, and the divisor is 8 rather than 10: getShapeAmount returns shapeControlTaper(shapeKnob * (cv / 8)). So a patched cable resting at 0V, or any negative voltage, holds the morph at zero and leaves the knob dead, and the knob is only reached at 8V. The EXPO jack has no attenuator and is summed into the same exponent as V/OCT, so despite the panel calling it exponential FM it tracks a volt per octave exactly as the pitch input does. The S GATE jack is normalled to 10V, so the sub runs whenever nothing is patched, and a patched cable held low silences the SUB output. The FREQ knob covers 10Hz to 10000Hz while the pitch as a whole is clamped to 8Hz to 20000Hz, so modulation can reach a little beyond either end of the knob. The OCT button and the Coarse Tune menu items set the same parameter. The waveform display is a plain widget with no parameter behind it.

lines: Replaces Rack's module browser with one that builds and stores every module's preview picture ahead of time, so scrolling the browser does not stall
Note — the module has no jacks and no knobs; placing it in the rack is the whole of using it, and taking it out puts the ordinary browser back
Note — the pictures are kept on disk under Leviathan/Deepcache in the Rack user folder and survive restarts, so the long first build happens once
Note — the lamps report what the caching is doing and the bar below them fills as it goes; they cannot be clicked
Note — a second copy of this module does nothing, and it stands aside entirely if another plugin has already replaced the browser, saying so on its menu
Menu — Rebuild cache — throws away every stored preview and builds them all again
Menu — Cache resolution — picks whether previews are stored at normal size or at double, which is sharper when browser cards are enlarged and takes about four times the memory
Menu — UI work budget: 0.5 ms, 1 ms, 2 ms, 4 ms, 8 ms — sets how long each drawn frame may spend building previews, trading a faster build for a smoother window
Menu — Cache statistics — reports how many previews are done, how many failed, how much memory they take and how long each one took to build
Deepcache.notes: Leviathan 2.9.1 source (commit c37193d, branch puffy-rc3): Deepcache.cpp declares no parameters, inputs or outputs, so the entry is a first line, notes and menu items. Cache resolution is a plugin-wide setting held in Leviathan/Deepcache/settings.json rather than patch state, because changing it rebuilds the shared database. The module detects Stoermelder's MB and any other plugin that has taken the browser, and prints the conflict on its own menu instead of fighting for it.

lines: An oscillator that turns a picture into a wavetable: each row of the image becomes one waveform, and a scan control sweeps down the rows
Sets the pitch, from 10Hz at the far left to 10000Hz at the far right, and starts at 261.63Hz; in LFO mode the same travel covers 0.01Hz to 100Hz
Detunes the oscillator by up to a hundred cents either side of the pitch set by FREQ
Snaps FREQ to whole octaves above and below middle C instead of letting it run smoothly, and starts off
Picks what the SYNC jack does: in the up position an edge restarts the waveform from the beginning, in the down position it reverses the direction of travel instead
Drops the pitch range to 0.01Hz through 100Hz, so the module works as a modulation source rather than an oscillator
Chooses which row of the picture is read as the waveform, the top row at the far left and the bottom row at the far right
Sets how much of the voltage at the SCAN jack is added to the SCAN knob, and reverses its sign anticlockwise of centre; at centre the jack does nothing
Sets how much of the voltage at the LIN FM jack reaches the frequency, none at the far left
Steps through which part of the picture's colour becomes the waveform: all three together, then red, then green, then blue; the four lamps beside it say which is chosen
Opens a short menu choosing where the picture comes from: an image file you pick, or the Nautiloid placed to the left of this module

Opens the settings that turn the picture into waveforms: two smoothing sliders, how the rows are levelled, which way up they are read, whether flat rows are trimmed, and whether the result is inverted
Sets the pitch at a volt per octave, added to FREQ and FINE; the number of channels on this jack sets how many voices the module runs
Modulates the frequency as a fraction of the current pitch, scaled by the LIN FM knob; the signal is stripped of any steady offset first, so only its swing counts
Moves the scan down and up the picture, ten volts covering the whole image at the attenuverter's full setting; it is added to the SCAN knob and the total is held between the top and bottom rows
A rising edge above 1V restarts the waveform, or reverses it when SOFT is chosen
The row of the picture chosen by SCAN, read as a waveform at the pitch the module is set to, swinging ±5V
The same waveform a quarter of a cycle ahead of OUT, swinging ±5V
Note — with no picture loaded the module makes sound anyway: the built-in table sweeps sine to triangle to saw to square as SCAN is turned, which is also what Clear image puts back
Note — the upper dark rectangle shows the picture the wavetable was made from, and the lower one draws the waveform currently being read; neither can be clicked
Note — to use a fractal instead of a file, place a Nautiloid immediately to the left and choose it from the source button; panning and zooming the fractal then reshapes the table as you go
Menu — Load image... — opens a file chooser for the picture the wavetable is built from
Menu — Reload image — reads the picture off disk again, picking up any change made to the file
Menu — Clear image — throws the picture away and goes back to the built-in sine, triangle, saw and square table
Menu — Embed image source in patch — saves the picture inside the patch file, so the patch sounds right on a machine that does not have the image
Menu — Seam smoothing — a slider setting how much the join between the end and start of each waveform is rounded off
Menu — Wave smoothing — a slider setting how much each waveform is smoothed along its length, trading detail for a quieter tone; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Menu — Normalize: Balanced, Global, Per row, Off — sets how the levels of the rows are evened out; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Menu — Row order: Top to bottom, Bottom to top — sets which end of the picture SCAN starts at; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Menu — Trim flat rows: Off, Gentle, Medium, Aggressive — drops rows of the picture with too little variation to make a waveform; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Menu — Per-row DC removal — takes the steady offset out of each row, so no waveform is off centre; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Menu — Invert conversion — turns the picture's light and dark the other way round before the waveforms are made; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu

Iris.notes: The scan total is a sum of knob and attenuated jack clamped to the ends of the table, so the attenuverter at centre leaves the SCAN jack inert; that is the one place a patched cable looks dead. The SCAN sumRange is written as the voltage the knob-plus-jack total is worth, since the clamp itself is on the row index. Three of the panel's buttons open menus of their own rather than doing anything themselves, and the lines written as Menu items for them say so: the smoothing, normalize, row order, trim, DC removal and invert items are all on the image-options button's menu, not on the module's right-click menu. The FREQ knob covers 10Hz to 10000Hz, or 0.01Hz to 100Hz in LFO mode, while the pitch as a whole is clamped to 8Hz to 20000Hz and to 45 per cent of the sample rate. The wavetable is never empty: the constructor fills it with a sine-triangle-saw-square sweep, so the module makes sound with no file loaded. Nautiloid is read from leftExpander, so it goes to the left of Iris. The picture preview, the waveform display and the preview toggle beside them are plain widgets with no parameter behind them.

lines: A fractal explorer whose picture is handed to an Iris oscillator as its wavetable source, so panning and zooming the fractal reshapes the sound
Opens a list of the fourteen built-in fractals and draws the one you pick
Puts the view back to the whole fractal, at the starting zoom and centre
Zooms the view in and out continuously while a voltage is present, +10V zooming in at full speed, -10V out at full speed and 0V leaving the view where it is
Pans the view sideways at a speed set by the voltage, +10V moving right at full speed, -10V left, and 0V leaving the view where it is
Pans the view up and down at a speed set by the voltage, +10V moving one way at full speed, -10V the other, and 0V leaving the view where it is
Note — this module is marked hidden in the plugin, so it does not appear in Rack's module browser; the way to get one is the Iris right-click menu, which adds it
Note — place it immediately to the left of an Iris, not to the right; Iris only reads a Nautiloid that is its left neighbour
Note — drag the picture to pan, and use the mouse wheel over it to zoom; neither gesture can be clicked for its own note, because the picture is one drawn widget
Note — LOC CODE is a sixteen-character code for where you are in the fractal; the two small buttons beside it copy it to the clipboard and paste one back, which is how a view is shared

Nautiloid.notes: Leviathan 2.9.1 source (commit c37193d, branch puffy-rc3): the module is listed with "hidden": true in the installed plugin.json, so it cannot be found in the module browser. Nautiloid checks rightExpander.module and requires that module's leftExpander to point back at it, so it is an expander that sits to the LEFT of the module it feeds, which is the opposite of the usual Rack convention; it feeds Iris, and Integral Flux uses it too, for the artwork behind the panel glass. Both buttons carry no printed label. The fractal picture, the location-code readout and the two clipboard buttons are plain widgets with no parameter behind them, so no click on them reaches this feature. A voltage smaller than 0.15V on any of the three jacks is treated as still, because the rate is tested against a 0.015 dead band after being divided by 10.

lines: A stereo saturator with seven distortion characters, a limiter on the way out, and a puffer fish that shows how hard it is being driven

Sets how much of the voltage at the PUFF jack is added to the PUFF knob, and reverses its sign anticlockwise of centre; at centre the jack does nothing
Adjusts the level going into the saturation without changing the level coming out, 6dB quieter at the far left and 6dB louder at the far right, and starts at the centre where it does nothing

Lets the fish leave the panel and swim about the rack, avoiding the mouse pointer and other Puffies; it starts off and nothing about the sound changes

The right channel of the signal to be saturated; with nothing patched into IN L this signal is sent to both channels

The right channel of the mix of dry and saturated signal, after the limiter
Note — with nothing patched into either input the module puts out silence; the fish is drawn and reacts to the controls all the same
Note — the fish is a meter: how far it inflates shows the drive reaching the saturation, how it moves shows the swing of the input, and its blush shows the limiter pulling the level down
Note — the fish picture and the waveform panel below it are drawn widgets, not controls, and no click on either reaches a note of its own
Menu — Roaming Mode — the same switch the roam button makes, letting the fish swim out of the panel and about the rack
Menu — Auto Deflate — pulls the output level down as PUFF is raised, by an amount fixed per character, so turning up the drive does not also turn up the volume

Puffy.notes: The PUFF sumRange is written as the voltage the knob-plus-jack total is worth, since the clamp itself is on the drive amount. The maker's own tooltips name the two character switches "Character (negative/linked)" and "Character (positive)", which is the clearest statement anywhere of what they do: the panel prints neither name. While the link switch is on, synchronizeCharacterSelectionFromUi copies one selector onto the other, so turning the positive one has no lasting effect; it comes up linked. The maker's own specification in doc/puffy.md lists six characters and calls BLOOM the default; the shipped build has seven, with TEETH added, and the specification is behind the code. The roaming fish, the roaming range bar and the waveform panel all sit in custom widgets; the range bar is a real ParamWidget and can be clicked, the fish and the waveform panel cannot. Roaming and the limiter mode are held outside the parameter system in the module's own JSON, so the limiter button reports its state only through its lamps.
